answer: The seat is earned with loss adjuster licence: a licence the institute renews after settled claims. A farm faking 260 aliases needs 260 separate verifiable records of this kind, each checked against the issuing authority, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The ripple check runs in the open: 260 fakes pay the full price 260 times, one honest agent pays once, and the reef trail in the ledger makes the gale cost visible to everyone.
